questions.def: Inversion requires 'hardly/scarcely/no sooner' + had + subject + past participle.
questions.question: ___ had I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: Inversion replaces 'if' in conditional sentences for emphasis/formality.
questions.question: ___, I would have said something.

questions.def: 'Never' requires inversion: Never have I seen...
questions.question: Never I have seen such a mess.

questions.def: Adverbs like 'seldom' require subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: ___ do we see such dedication.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' begins an inverted sentence for emphasis.
questions.question: ___ circumstances should you open this package.

questions.def: 'Only then' triggers inversion because it's an adverbial phrase.
questions.question: Only ___ did I understand the problem.

questions.def: 'Little' (meaning almost nothing) triggers inversion.
questions.question: ___ did they know what was coming.

questions.def: 'Only now' is an adverbial phrase that triggers inversion.
questions.question: ___ I realize the importance of this issue.

questions.def: 'No sooner...than' requires inversion in the 'no sooner' clause.
questions.question: ___ did she leave than he arrived.

questions.def: 'Rarely' requires subject-verb inversion: Rarely has she seen...
questions.question: Rarely she has seen such beauty in nature.

questions.def: 'Scarcely...when' uses inversion; similar to 'hardly' and 'no sooner'.
questions.question: ___ had we started when it rained.

questions.def: 'Were that' replaces 'if' in conditional sentences, causing inversion.
questions.question: ___ the case, I will support your decision.

questions.def: 'Had' begins an inverted conditional, replacing 'If I had known'.
questions.question: ___ I known it was her birthday, I'd have baked a cake.

questions.def: 'Never' requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: ___ have I felt so disappointed.

questions.def: 'Little' (meaning almost nothing) requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ did I expect to see him here.

questions.def: 'Not since then' requires inversion because it's an adverbial phrase.
questions.question: Not since ___ have I felt so content.

questions.def: 'Only after' triggers inversion of the subject and auxiliary verb.
questions.question: ___ after the meeting did I understand.

questions.def: 'No sooner...than' is an inverted structure.
questions.question: ___ I finished my work than I went out.

questions.def: 'Should' replaces 'If' in inverted conditional clauses.
questions.question: ___ should you require assistance, please contact us.

questions.def: 'Hardly' requires inversion: Hardly had he started...
questions.question: Hardly he had started eating when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Nowhere' requires subject-verb inversion for emphasis.
questions.question: ___ have I seen such beauty.

questions.def: 'Scarcely...when' requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ had he left when she arrived.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires inversion.
questions.question: Under ___ circumstances are you allowed to leave.

questions.def: 'On no account' requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ no account are you to do that.

questions.def: 'Little' triggers inversion.
questions.question: ___ had I anticipated such a disaster.

questions.def: 'Were that to happen' uses inversion to replace 'if'.
questions.question: Were ___ to happen, we'd be in trouble.

questions.def: Inversions require auxiliary verb before subject after negative adverbials.
questions.question: Never ___ I seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: After 'only after,' auxiliary verb precedes the subject.
questions.question: Only after finishing the project ___ I realize my mistake.

questions.def: 'Scarcely/Hardly...when' use past perfect; invert 'had'.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ the bell rung when everyone left. (has)

questions.def: Negative adverbial 'under no circumstances' requires subject-verb inversion.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ you to open this file.
